text:
anya: alert from the backup-integrity job — a small batch of incremental snapshots show missing SSE-KMS headers in S3. noticed during verify-run at 01:02 UTC.
deploy-bot: [alert] 4912345678: s3-put-object without x-amz-server-side-encryption (count=9).
anya: short version: uploader service-account temporarily lost kms:Encrypt on the CMK used for snapshot encryption. looks like a narrow time window (~3m).
devon: running quick cloudtrail grep now — searching PutObject events for bucket redwood-snaps and absent ServerSideEncryption field.
devon: (log excerpt) 
```
2024-11-04T01:02:13Z PutObject userIdentity.arn=arn:aws:sts::111:assumed-role/backup-uploader/... requestParameters.bucketName=redwood-snaps x-amz-server-side-encryption=null
2024-11-04T01:03:55Z PutObject userIdentity.arn=arn:aws:sts::111:assumed-role/backup-uploader/... requestParameters.bucketName=redwood-snaps x-amz-server-side-encryption=null
```
anya: exact pattern. appears to coincide with a role policy change that landed earlier today.
morgan: which PR? I can look at policy diff and confirm if kms:Encrypt was removed vs scoped away.
chris: PR #7892 touched module roles: backup-uploader — we scoped a permissive kms grant to a narrower resource pattern for tenant-tagged objects. bad interaction: the CMK grant we expected to cover snapshot prefix uses a condition on aws:ResourceTag, but backup agent uses a different tag key during incremental writes. So the grant effectively didn't match for these objects.
sara: taking on immediate mitigations: 1) pause snapshot uploads (set routing flag) 2) reapply a permissive grant to restore writes 3) scan and mark objects missing SSE. I'll run step 2 now.
sara: running
```
# re-create ephemeral grant to let uploader write until we fix policy
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/redwood-snaps-cmk --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::111:role/backup-uploader --operations Encrypt,Decrypt
```
chris: good. can we also add an InlinePolicy patch to the role as temporary fast fix while we propagate Terraform rollback?
anya: yep — patching role directly to restore kms:Encrypt for the sa. patch applied at 01:09 UTC.
devon: now scanning S3 to enumerate affected objects (no SSE flag). using inventory is faster but we have a small set. quick aws s3api list-objects-v2 + head-object check.
devon: script snippet:
```
aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket redwood-snaps --prefix incremental/2024-11-04/ --query 'Contents[].Key' | xargs -n1 -I{} sh -c "aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-snaps --key '{}' --query '{Key: Key, SSE: ServerSideEncryption}'"
```
devon: found 9 objects with SSE null.
anya: plan for those objects: copy over themselves with SSE-KMS to re-encrypt in-place (S3 Copy with --server-side-encryption aws:kms). This is idempotent and preserves metadata.
sara: I'm running the copy re-encrypt now in a controlled loop. throttling at 2r/s. progress: 6/9 done.
morgan: audit / compliance notes — we need to capture exact time window, list of affected tenant IDs, and whether any cleartext snapshots left the system. so far only S3 lacked SSE header; objects were uploaded but were still encrypted locally before upload? devon: agent side does client-side encryption? no, we rely on SSE-KMS at server side. so objects during the gap were stored in S3 without KMS envelope. need to assume they were not encrypted at rest.
chris: check EBS/db snapshots — unaffected; this is only S3 snapshot store.
devon: running an Athena query against S3 access logs to get requester IPs and object sizes.
devon: quick CloudTrail query for PutObject events returns the list of request IDs for cross-check.
morgan: notify legal/compliance with initial incident summary. low blast radius but treat as P1 for compliance.
anya: immediate followups: 
- complete re-encrypt of affected objects (in progress)
- revert PR #7892 or correct condition attr to match agent tagging (tomorrow EOD)
- add CI check that verifies CMK grants and tag condition match expected upload tags
- add an on-write assertion that rejects PutObject without SSE header (or enforce bucket policy requiring sse:kms)
- run full inventory to find any other time windows with similar patterns
devon: suggested bucket policy snippet to block non-sse uploads: 
```
{
  "Sid": "DenyNonSSE",
  "Effect": "Deny",
  "Principal": "*",
  "Action": "s3:PutObject",
  "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::redwood-snaps/*",
  "Condition": {
    "StringNotEquals": {"s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption": "aws:kms"}
  }
}
```
chris: add that as short-term enforcement; will require us to ensure all existing clients send SSE header or use bucket-side enforcement with kms key policy. I'll submit a hotfix.
sara: re-encrypt finished: 9/9 done at 01:17 UTC. verifying checksums now.
anya: nice. please attach the list of affected object keys and cloudtrail event IDs to the incident ticket.
morgan: logging actionable items in INC-2024-1043 and pinging legal. also scheduling a follow-up postmortem next week.
anya: long-term: change CMK grant pattern to rely on principal + explicit resource ARNs (avoid fragile tag conditions for uploader flow), add acceptance test that deploys minimal role + CMK to simulate writes, and include an audit query (CloudTrail rule) that alerts when PutObject without SSE occurs.
devon: also adding a runbook step to check for policy/tag drift before merging role policy changes.
sara: oncall handing off — will follow up in the PM. :thumbsup: 
chris: thanks everyone. closing loop once postmortem draft is up. :white_check_mark:
